questions.prompt: The ____ system coordinates all the activities of the body.
questions.explanation: The nervous system coordinates body activities.

questions.prompt: The nervous system is a network of billions of nerve cells called ____.
questions.explanation: Neurons are the nerve cells of the nervous system.

questions.prompt: Neurons carry ____ throughout the body to control its activities.
questions.explanation: Neurons carry signals throughout the body.

questions.prompt: ____ means all parts of the body work together in an organized way.
questions.explanation: Coordination is organized teamwork of body parts.

questions.prompt: ____ of nerves are spread throughout the entire human body.
questions.explanation: Millions of nerves form the body's network.

questions.prompt: The CNS is made up of the brain and the ____ ____.
questions.explanation: The CNS is the brain and spinal cord.

questions.prompt: CNS stands for Central ____ System.
questions.explanation: CNS = Central Nervous System.

questions.prompt: PNS stands for ____ Nervous System.
questions.explanation: PNS = Peripheral Nervous System.

questions.prompt: Receptors and effectors are connected to the CNS by ____.
questions.explanation: Nerves connect receptors and effectors to the CNS.

questions.prompt: The CNS is the control center; the PNS is the ____ network.
questions.explanation: The PNS carries messages to and from the CNS.

questions.prompt: The spinal cord runs down through the backbone, also called the ____ column.
questions.explanation: The spinal cord runs through the vertebral column.

questions.prompt: The spinal cord acts as the main communication ____ between brain and body.
questions.explanation: It is the communication highway of the body.

questions.prompt: The spinal cord runs from the ____ down through the backbone.
questions.explanation: It runs from the medulla (brainstem) downwards.

questions.prompt: The brain is located inside the ____.
questions.explanation: The brain sits inside the skull (cranium).

questions.prompt: ____ fluid cushions and protects the brain from shocks.
questions.explanation: Cerebrospinal fluid protects the brain.

questions.prompt: The wrinkles on the brain increase its ____ area so more cells fit.
questions.explanation: Folds increase surface area for more neurons.

questions.prompt: The three basic parts of the brain are the forebrain, ____ and hindbrain.
questions.explanation: The three parts are forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain.

questions.prompt: Even during sleep, the brain stays ____.
questions.explanation: The brain remains active during sleep.

questions.prompt: Besides protecting the brain, CSF provides ____ and removes waste.
questions.explanation: CSF supplies nutrients and removes waste.

questions.prompt: The brain is the body's ____ center.
questions.explanation: The brain is the control center of the body.

questions.prompt: Sense organs send collected information first to the ____.
questions.explanation: The thalamus receives sensory information first.

questions.prompt: Unlike a computer, the brain can feel ____ and think creatively.
questions.explanation: The brain can feel emotions, unlike a computer.

questions.prompt: The brain works like a highly advanced ____.
questions.explanation: The brain is compared to an advanced computer.

questions.prompt: The ____ is the largest and most developed part of the brain.
questions.explanation: The forebrain is the largest, most developed part.

questions.prompt: The forebrain consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and ____.
questions.explanation: Its parts are cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus.

questions.prompt: The cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus make up the ____.
questions.explanation: These three form the forebrain.

questions.prompt: The ____ is the largest part of the human brain.
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is the largest brain part.

questions.prompt: The cerebrum is the ____ part of the brain.
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is the thinking part.

questions.prompt: The two halves of the cerebrum are called cerebral ____.
questions.explanation: They are the cerebral hemispheres.

questions.prompt: The right cerebral hemisphere controls the ____ side of the body.
questions.explanation: The right hemisphere controls the left side.

questions.prompt: The left cerebral hemisphere controls the ____ side of the body.
questions.explanation: The left hemisphere controls the right side.

questions.prompt: Language and logical thinking are controlled by the ____ hemisphere.
questions.explanation: The left hemisphere handles language and logic.

questions.prompt: Creativity and artistic ability are controlled by the ____ hemisphere.
questions.explanation: The right hemisphere handles creativity and art.

questions.prompt: The wrinkled outer layer of the cerebrum is the cerebral ____.
questions.explanation: The outer layer is the cerebral cortex.

questions.prompt: The ____ cortex controls voluntary body movements.
questions.explanation: The motor cortex controls voluntary movement.

questions.prompt: The ____ cortex processes touch, pain and temperature.
questions.explanation: The sensory cortex processes body sensations.

questions.prompt: The ____ cortex processes hearing.
questions.explanation: The auditory cortex processes sound.

questions.prompt: The ____ cortex processes vision.
questions.explanation: The visual cortex processes sight.

questions.prompt: Muscles we can consciously control are called ____ muscles.
questions.explanation: Voluntary muscles are under conscious control.

questions.prompt: The thalamus acts as a ____ station for the brain.
questions.explanation: The thalamus is a relay station.

questions.prompt: The thalamus relays sensory information to the ____.
questions.explanation: It forwards sensory signals to the cerebrum.

questions.prompt: The thalamus is located inside the ____ (brain division).
questions.explanation: The thalamus is part of the forebrain.

questions.prompt: Relaying means passing on ____ to the correct part of the cerebrum.
questions.explanation: Relaying is forwarding messages onward.

questions.prompt: The hypothalamus acts as the body's ____.
questions.explanation: It works as the body's thermostat.

questions.prompt: Normal human body temperature is about ____ °C.
questions.explanation: Normal body temperature is about 37°C.

questions.prompt: When the body is too hot, the hypothalamus triggers ____.
questions.explanation: Sweating cools the body when it is hot.

questions.prompt: When the body is too cold, the hypothalamus triggers ____.
questions.explanation: Shivering warms the body when it is cold.

questions.prompt: The hypothalamus controls the ____ gland.
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus controls the pituitary gland.

questions.prompt: Sweat ____ from the skin absorbs heat and cools the body.
questions.explanation: Evaporation of sweat removes heat.

questions.prompt: The ____ is the smallest and most central part of the brain.
questions.explanation: The midbrain is the smallest, central part.

questions.prompt: The midbrain connects the forebrain to the ____.
questions.explanation: It bridges the forebrain and hindbrain.

questions.prompt: The three parts of the brainstem are the midbrain, pons and ____.
questions.explanation: The brainstem is midbrain, pons and medulla.

questions.prompt: The midbrain acts as a ____ between the forebrain and hindbrain.
questions.explanation: It is a bridge between the two regions.

questions.prompt: The hindbrain is the ____ part of the brain.
questions.explanation: The hindbrain is the lower part.

questions.prompt: The hindbrain consists of the cerebellum, medulla and ____.
questions.explanation: Its parts are cerebellum, medulla and pons.

questions.prompt: The cerebellum controls balance and ____ movement.
questions.explanation: It controls balance and coordinated movement.

questions.prompt: The cerebellum lets us perform ____ movements almost automatically.
questions.explanation: It stores learned movement patterns.

questions.prompt: The cerebellum is found at the ____ and bottom of the brain.
questions.explanation: It is at the back and bottom, below the cerebrum.

questions.prompt: Damage to the cerebellum causes loss of ____.
questions.explanation: Cerebellum damage causes loss of balance.

questions.prompt: The medulla controls involuntary actions such as breathing and ____.
questions.explanation: It controls breathing, heartbeat and peristalsis.

questions.prompt: ____ is the wave-like muscle contraction that moves food along the gut.
questions.explanation: Peristalsis pushes food through the digestive tract.

questions.prompt: Breathing is an ____ action that happens automatically.
questions.explanation: Breathing is involuntary.

questions.prompt: Involuntary muscles are found in the heart and ____ system.
questions.explanation: They are in the heart, ribcage and digestive system.

questions.prompt: The medulla is also called the ____.
questions.explanation: The medulla is also known as the brainstem.

questions.prompt: The pons is a structure found in the ____.
questions.explanation: The pons is part of the hindbrain.

questions.prompt: The pons acts as a ____ between the spinal cord and the brain.
questions.explanation: It links the spinal cord and brain.

questions.prompt: The pituitary gland produces ____ (chemical messengers).
questions.explanation: It produces hormones.

questions.prompt: The pituitary is called the ____ gland because it controls other glands.
questions.explanation: It is called the master gland.

questions.prompt: The pituitary gland is located just below the ____.
questions.explanation: It sits below the hypothalamus.

questions.prompt: The pituitary produces ____ hormone that controls how fast the body grows.
questions.explanation: Growth hormone controls body growth rate.

questions.prompt: Hormones are chemical ____ released by glands.
questions.explanation: Hormones are chemical messengers.

questions.prompt: A ____ is any change in the environment that the body detects and reacts to.
questions.explanation: A stimulus is a detected change.

questions.prompt: A ____ is the body's reaction to a stimulus.
questions.explanation: A response is the reaction to a stimulus.

questions.prompt: Sweating is the body's response to the stimulus of increased ____.
questions.explanation: Rising temperature causes sweating.

questions.prompt: Hunger is a stimulus, and ____ is the response.
questions.explanation: Eating is the response to hunger.

questions.prompt: An itch is a stimulus, and ____ is the response.
questions.explanation: Scratching is the response to an itch.

questions.prompt: The faster an animal responds to stimuli, the better its chance of ____.
questions.explanation: Fast responses improve survival.

questions.prompt: ____ are specialized structures that detect stimuli.
questions.explanation: Receptors detect stimuli.

questions.prompt: Receptors convert a stimulus into a ____ sent to the brain.
questions.explanation: They turn stimuli into signals.

questions.prompt: ____ are the body parts that carry out the response to a stimulus.
questions.explanation: Effectors carry out responses.

questions.prompt: In multicellular organisms, the effectors are ____.
questions.explanation: Muscles are the effectors.

questions.prompt: In short: receptors DETECT and effectors ____.
questions.explanation: Receptors detect; effectors act.

questions.prompt: For a nearby object, the eye lens becomes ____.
questions.explanation: The lens thickens for near objects.

questions.prompt: For a distant object, the eye lens becomes ____.
questions.explanation: The lens thins for distant objects.

questions.prompt: The ____ is an example of a complex sense organ that acts as a receptor.
questions.explanation: The eye, ear and nose are complex sense organs.

questions.prompt: Muscles act as effectors by contracting or ____.
questions.explanation: Muscles contract or relax to respond.

questions.prompt: A ____ is the basic working unit of the nervous system.
questions.explanation: The neuron is the basic unit.

questions.prompt: Neurons carry electrical signals called ____.
questions.explanation: They carry electrical impulses.

questions.prompt: The ____ ____ of a neuron contains the nucleus.
questions.explanation: The nucleus is in the cell body.

questions.prompt: ____ receive signals and carry them towards the cell body.
questions.explanation: Dendrites carry signals to the cell body.

questions.prompt: The ____ carries signals away from the cell body.
questions.explanation: The axon sends signals away from the cell body.

questions.prompt: The ____ sheath is the fatty insulation around the axon.
questions.explanation: The myelin sheath insulates the axon.

questions.prompt: Signals pass to the next neuron at the axon ____.
questions.explanation: Axon terminals pass signals on.

questions.prompt: Nerve impulses travel in ____ direction only.
questions.explanation: Impulses travel one way.

questions.prompt: The myelin sheath is like ____ insulation around an electrical wire.
questions.explanation: Myelin is like plastic on a wire.

questions.prompt: The two types of nerve cells are ____ and motor neurons.
questions.explanation: Sensory and motor are the two types.

questions.prompt: ____ neurons carry impulses from receptors to the CNS.
questions.explanation: Sensory neurons carry signals into the CNS.

questions.prompt: ____ neurons carry impulses from the CNS to muscles and glands.
questions.explanation: Motor neurons carry commands to effectors.

questions.prompt: Sensory neurons inform the brain; motor neurons ____ the body to act.
questions.explanation: Motor neurons command the body.

questions.prompt: A ____ is a bundle of many nerve fibres (axons).
questions.explanation: A nerve is a bundle of axons.

questions.prompt: A nerve containing both sensory and motor cells is called a ____ nerve.
questions.explanation: Both types together make a mixed nerve.

questions.prompt: Without myelin, nerve signals would ____ out and slow down.
questions.explanation: Myelin prevents leakage of signals.

questions.prompt: In the cable comparison, the axons are like the metal ____.
questions.explanation: Axons are like the wires; myelin is the coating.

questions.prompt: Myelin helps ____ up the transmission of nerve impulses.
questions.explanation: Myelin speeds up impulse transmission.

questions.prompt: ____ actions require conscious thought and are deliberately chosen.
questions.explanation: Voluntary actions are conscious and chosen.

questions.prompt: ____ actions happen automatically and very fast without conscious thought.
questions.explanation: Reflex actions are automatic and fast.

questions.prompt: Reflex actions are fast because the ____ ____ coordinates them directly.
questions.explanation: The spinal cord handles reflexes.

questions.prompt: Voluntary actions are controlled by the ____.
questions.explanation: The cerebrum controls voluntary actions.

questions.prompt: The nerve pathway of a reflex action is called a reflex ____.
questions.explanation: The reflex arc is the reflex pathway.

questions.prompt: In a reflex arc, a ____ neuron in the spinal cord processes the signal.
questions.explanation: A relay neuron processes the signal.

questions.prompt: In bright light, the pupil becomes ____ to protect the retina.
questions.explanation: The pupil shrinks in bright light.

questions.prompt: When food enters the windpipe, the reflex response is ____.
questions.explanation: Coughing clears the airway.

questions.prompt: When an insect touches the eyelid, the reflex is ____.
questions.explanation: Blinking protects the eye.

questions.prompt: Smelling food when hungry produces ____.
questions.explanation: The smell triggers saliva.

questions.prompt: Touching a newborn's palm triggers the ____ reflex.
questions.explanation: The gripping reflex makes the baby grip tightly.

questions.prompt: Baby reflexes are present from ____ without being learned.
questions.explanation: Babies are born with these reflexes.

questions.prompt: A ____ is the tiny gap between two neurons.
questions.explanation: The synapse is the gap between neurons.

questions.prompt: A signal crosses a synapse using a chemical messenger called a ____.
questions.explanation: A neurotransmitter carries the signal across.

questions.prompt: At a synapse the chemical crosses the gap by ____.
questions.explanation: The chemical diffuses across the gap.

questions.prompt: Each neuron forms ____ of synaptic connections.
questions.explanation: Neurons form thousands of connections.

questions.prompt: The tiny gap between neurons is called the synaptic ____.
questions.explanation: It is the synaptic gap.

questions.prompt: When a nerve is cut, signal ____ between brain and muscles is blocked.
questions.explanation: A cut nerve blocks signal transmission.

questions.prompt: If a motor nerve is damaged, muscles may become ____.
questions.explanation: Damaged motor nerves cause paralysis.

questions.prompt: Nerves in the CNS have very limited ability to ____ themselves.
questions.explanation: CNS nerve damage is often permanent.

questions.prompt: If a sensory nerve is cut, the person feels no ____ in that area.
questions.explanation: Loss of sensation follows sensory nerve damage.

questions.prompt: ____ is the brain's main energy source.
questions.explanation: The brain runs mainly on glucose.

questions.prompt: The brain is approximately ____ % water.
questions.explanation: The brain is about 75% water.

questions.prompt: Illegal drugs produce ____ that destroy neurons.
questions.explanation: Neurotoxins are poisonous to nerve cells.

questions.prompt: Even mild ____ reduces concentration and memory.
questions.explanation: Dehydration harms concentration and memory.

questions.prompt: To stay healthy, the brain needs glucose, ____ and water.
questions.explanation: Glucose, vitamins and water keep it healthy.

questions.prompt: The brain and spinal cord together form the ____ Nervous System.
questions.explanation: They form the Central Nervous System.

questions.prompt: The two main divisions of the nervous system are the CNS and the ____.
questions.explanation: They are the CNS and PNS.

questions.prompt: The brain is a wrinkled, ____ organ.
questions.explanation: The brain is greyish and wrinkled.

questions.prompt: The cerebrum controls conscious thoughts, reasoning, memory and ____.
questions.explanation: It controls emotions among other things.

questions.prompt: Damage to the left hemisphere can cause loss of ____ and language.
questions.explanation: Left-hemisphere damage affects speech.

questions.prompt: Shivering produces ____ that warms the body.
questions.explanation: Muscle contractions in shivering produce heat.

questions.prompt: Signals travelling up through the midbrain carry ____ information.
questions.explanation: Upward signals carry sensory information.

questions.prompt: Signals travelling down through the midbrain carry ____ commands.
questions.explanation: Downward signals carry motor commands.

questions.prompt: With practice, the cerebellum lets actions run without conscious ____.
questions.explanation: Practised actions become automatic.

questions.prompt: In peristalsis, muscles behind the food ____ while those in front relax.
questions.explanation: Contraction behind and relaxation in front push food along.

questions.prompt: Peristalsis occurs throughout the ____ canal.
questions.explanation: It occurs along the alimentary canal.

questions.prompt: Receptors detect changes and send information to the ____.
questions.explanation: Receptors send signals to the brain.

questions.prompt: The nucleus in the cell body controls all the neuron's ____.
questions.explanation: The nucleus controls cell activities.

questions.prompt: We feel pain a moment after a reflex because a signal reaches the ____ afterwards.
questions.explanation: The brain is informed after the reflex.

questions.prompt: Chemical synapses ensure ____-way communication.
questions.explanation: Synapses ensure one-way communication.

questions.prompt: Spinal cord injuries often cause loss of ____.
questions.explanation: They can cause loss of movement.

questions.prompt: Challenging mental activities stimulate new ____ between neurons.
questions.explanation: They build new neural connections.

questions.prompt: Too little growth hormone in a child can cause ____ growth.
questions.explanation: Low growth hormone slows growth.

questions.prompt: If the thalamus is damaged, a person may experience loss of ____.
questions.explanation: Thalamus damage impairs sensation.

questions.prompt: From the cerebrum, commands travel down the ____ ____ to the muscles.
questions.explanation: Commands go down the spinal cord to muscles.

questions.prompt: The nervous system ____ all the activities of the body.
questions.explanation: It coordinates and controls body activities.

questions.prompt: Nerve cells are also called ____.
questions.explanation: Nerve cells are neurons.

questions.prompt: Coordination means body parts work together in a ____ way.
questions.explanation: They work in a controlled, organized way.

questions.prompt: The spinal cord and the ____ form the CNS.
questions.explanation: The CNS is the brain and spinal cord.

questions.prompt: The PNS connects the CNS to receptors and ____.
questions.explanation: It links the CNS to receptors and effectors.

questions.prompt: The CNS receives, processes and sends ____ to control the body.
questions.explanation: It sends commands back to the body.

questions.prompt: Together, the brain and spinal cord coordinate all activities of the ____.
questions.explanation: They coordinate all body activities.

questions.prompt: The skull is also called the ____.
questions.explanation: The skull is the cranium.

questions.prompt: The folds on the brain let more brain ____ fit inside the skull.
questions.explanation: More neurons fit due to the folds.

questions.prompt: During sleep the brain keeps controlling breathing and ____.
questions.explanation: It controls vital functions during sleep.

questions.prompt: The brain stores ____, analyzes information and makes decisions.
questions.explanation: It stores memory and makes decisions.

questions.prompt: The thalamus relays sensory information to the ____ for processing.
questions.explanation: The thalamus passes signals to the cerebrum.

questions.prompt: The largest part of the forebrain is the ____.
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is the largest forebrain part.

questions.prompt: The forebrain is the most highly ____ part of the brain.
questions.explanation: It is the most developed brain part.

questions.prompt: The cerebrum controls voluntary body ____.
questions.explanation: It controls voluntary movements.

questions.prompt: The left and ____ hemispheres make up the cerebrum.
questions.explanation: The two hemispheres are left and right.

questions.prompt: The motor cortex sends signals to the ____ to produce movement.
questions.explanation: It signals the muscles.

questions.prompt: Each area of the cerebral cortex is ____ to process a specific type of information.
questions.explanation: Cortex areas are specialized.

questions.prompt: An example of a voluntary movement is ____ a ball.
questions.explanation: Kicking a ball is a voluntary movement.

questions.prompt: The cerebral cortex is the ____ layer of the cerebrum.
questions.explanation: It is the outer layer.

questions.prompt: The thalamus is located just above the ____.
questions.explanation: It sits above the brainstem.

questions.prompt: The thalamus is called a relay ____.
questions.explanation: It is called a relay station.

questions.prompt: The thalamus also helps control body ____ and coordination.
questions.explanation: It helps control movement and coordination.

questions.prompt: The hypothalamus keeps body temperature stable at about 37 ____.
questions.explanation: It maintains about 37°C.

questions.prompt: The hypothalamus links the nervous system to the ____ system.
questions.explanation: It links to the endocrine system.

questions.prompt: When too hot, sweating releases ____ from the body.
questions.explanation: Sweating releases heat.

questions.prompt: The midbrain is the most ____ part of the brain.
questions.explanation: It is the central/middle part.

questions.prompt: The midbrain, pons and medulla form the ____.
questions.explanation: These three form the brainstem.

questions.prompt: The cerebellum, medulla and pons make up the ____.
questions.explanation: They form the hindbrain.

questions.prompt: The medulla and pons are parts of the ____.
questions.explanation: They belong to the brainstem.

questions.prompt: The cerebellum stores the ____ of a learned movement.
questions.explanation: It stores movement patterns.

questions.prompt: Damage to the cerebellum causes uncoordinated, ____ movements.
questions.explanation: Movements become shaky and inaccurate.

questions.prompt: Riding a bicycle and swimming are examples of ____ movements.
questions.explanation: They are learned movements.

questions.prompt: The medulla controls breathing, heartbeat and ____.
questions.explanation: It controls these involuntary actions.

questions.prompt: Peristalsis is controlled by the ____ nervous system.
questions.explanation: Peristalsis is autonomic (involuntary).

questions.prompt: Muscles that work automatically are called ____ muscles.
questions.explanation: Involuntary muscles work automatically.

questions.prompt: Damage to the medulla is extremely serious because it controls ____ functions.
questions.explanation: It controls vital functions.

questions.prompt: The pons helps ____ signals between the brain and the body.
questions.explanation: It transmits signals between brain and body.

questions.prompt: The pituitary regulates the amount of ____ in the body.
questions.explanation: It regulates water balance.

questions.prompt: The pituitary also regulates blood ____ levels.
questions.explanation: It regulates blood sugar.

questions.prompt: An increase in temperature during exercise is an example of a ____.
questions.explanation: It is a stimulus.

questions.prompt: Detecting danger and running away prevents ____.
questions.explanation: Responding to danger prevents harm.

questions.prompt: Detecting hunger and finding food prevents ____.
questions.explanation: It prevents starvation.

questions.prompt: Receptors detect both external and ____ changes.
questions.explanation: They detect internal and external changes.

questions.prompt: Pain receptors in the skin are ____-cell receptors.
questions.explanation: They are single-cell receptors.

questions.prompt: Eye muscles change the shape of the ____ to focus light.
questions.explanation: They change the lens shape to focus.

questions.prompt: The lens focuses light onto the ____ for sharp vision.
questions.explanation: Light is focused onto the retina.

questions.prompt: Some axons can be up to one ____ long.
questions.explanation: Some axons are up to a metre long.

questions.prompt: Impulses travel from dendrites to the cell body to the ____.
questions.explanation: They travel to the axon terminals.

questions.prompt: The myelin sheath prevents signal ____.
questions.explanation: Myelin prevents signal leakage.

questions.prompt: Dendrites are the ____ that receive incoming signals.
questions.explanation: Dendrites are branching extensions.

questions.prompt: Sensory neurons carry impulses towards the ____.
questions.explanation: They carry signals to the CNS.

questions.prompt: Motor neurons carry impulses to muscles and ____.
questions.explanation: They carry commands to muscles and glands.

questions.prompt: The body needs both neuron types for ____-way communication.
questions.explanation: Two-way communication needs both types.

questions.prompt: In a nerve, the myelin sheath is like the ____ coating on a wire.
questions.explanation: Myelin is like plastic coating.

questions.prompt: A nerve can contain only sensory cells, only motor cells, or ____ of both.
questions.explanation: It can be a mixture of both.

questions.prompt: Nerves carry signals to and from the brain and ____ ____.
questions.explanation: They connect to the brain and spinal cord.

questions.prompt: Reflex actions protect the body from ____.
questions.explanation: Reflexes protect from injury.

questions.prompt: In a reflex arc, the ____ detects the stimulus first.
questions.explanation: The receptor detects the stimulus first.

questions.prompt: In a reflex arc, the motor neuron carries the impulse to the ____.
questions.explanation: The motor neuron reaches the effector.

questions.prompt: Writing and speaking are examples of ____ actions.
questions.explanation: They are voluntary actions.

questions.prompt: The pupil shrinks in bright light to protect the ____.
questions.explanation: It protects the retina.

questions.prompt: Coughing clears the ____ when food enters the windpipe.
questions.explanation: Coughing clears the airway.

questions.prompt: Touching an electric wire makes the hand ____ away.
questions.explanation: The hand is pulled away by reflex.

questions.prompt: Inborn reflexes protect a baby and aid its ____.
questions.explanation: They aid the baby's survival.

questions.prompt: Examples of baby reflexes include gripping, sucking and ____.
questions.explanation: Gripping, sucking and blinking are baby reflexes.

questions.prompt: At a synapse, neurons do not ____ each other.
questions.explanation: Neurons do not touch; there is a gap.

questions.prompt: A nerve impulse reaching the axon ____ triggers the chemical's release.
questions.explanation: It is triggered at the axon terminal.

questions.prompt: The chemical reaches the ____ of the next neuron.
questions.explanation: It reaches the next neuron's dendrites.

questions.prompt: After motor nerve damage, muscles have no instructions to ____.
questions.explanation: Without signals, muscles cannot contract.

questions.prompt: A cut nerve may cause muscles to stop working, called ____.
questions.explanation: This is paralysis.

questions.prompt: Nerves are described as ____ because they are easily damaged.
questions.explanation: Nerves are fragile.

questions.prompt: The brain uses glucose to power its ____ activity and thinking.
questions.explanation: Glucose powers its electrical activity.

questions.prompt: Staying ____ helps nerve cells work efficiently.
questions.explanation: Hydration keeps nerve cells working well.

questions.prompt: Neurotoxins are chemicals that are ____ to nerve cells.
questions.explanation: Neurotoxins are poisonous to neurons.

questions.prompt: Learning new skills and solving ____ keep the brain sharp.
questions.explanation: Puzzles and new skills keep the brain sharp.

questions.prompt: The left hemisphere handles analytical skills and ____.
questions.explanation: It handles mathematics and analysis.

questions.prompt: The right hemisphere handles imagination and ____ ability.
questions.explanation: It handles musical/artistic ability.

questions.prompt: Shivering is caused by rapid ____ contractions.
questions.explanation: Rapid muscle contractions cause shivering.

questions.prompt: Peristalsis pushes food from one part of the ____ to another.
questions.explanation: It moves food along the gut.

questions.prompt: Vision, hearing and touch are routed through the ____ before the cortex.
questions.explanation: The thalamus routes senses to the cortex.

questions.prompt: The nervous system carries signals to control and ____ all body activities.
questions.explanation: It controls and coordinates activities.

questions.prompt: Neurons form a vast communication ____ throughout the body.
questions.explanation: Nerves form a communication network.

questions.prompt: The brain and spinal cord coordinate all ____ of the body.
questions.explanation: The CNS coordinates body activities.

questions.prompt: The PNS carries messages to and from the ____.
questions.explanation: The PNS links to the CNS.

questions.prompt: Cerebrospinal fluid acts as a shock ____ for the brain.
questions.explanation: CSF is a shock absorber.

questions.prompt: The brain is protected by the hard ____ bone.
questions.explanation: The skull protects the brain.

questions.prompt: The brain coordinates thinking, emotions and ____.
questions.explanation: It coordinates thinking, emotions and actions.

questions.prompt: Both a computer and the brain receive ____ and produce output.
questions.explanation: Both take input and give output.

questions.prompt: The thalamus and hypothalamus are parts of the ____.
questions.explanation: They are forebrain parts.

questions.prompt: The cerebrum is responsible for conscious ____ and reasoning.
questions.explanation: It handles conscious thought.

questions.prompt: Each cerebral hemisphere has specialized ____.
questions.explanation: Hemispheres have specialized functions.

questions.prompt: The cerebral cortex gives the brain its bumpy, ____ appearance.
questions.explanation: The cortex is wrinkled/folded.

questions.prompt: The sensory cortex receives signals about touch, pressure, pain and ____.
questions.explanation: It processes temperature too.

questions.prompt: The thalamus receives feedback from the cerebral ____.
questions.explanation: It gets feedback from the cortex.

questions.prompt: The thalamus sorts and relays ____ information.
questions.explanation: It relays sensory information.

questions.prompt: The hypothalamus is located at the ____ of the brain.
questions.explanation: It is at the base of the brain.

questions.prompt: In Fahrenheit, normal body temperature is about ____ °F.
questions.explanation: Normal temperature is 98.6°F.

questions.prompt: The hypothalamus also regulates thirst and ____.
questions.explanation: It regulates thirst and hunger.

questions.prompt: If the midbrain is damaged, signals between forebrain and hindbrain are ____.
questions.explanation: The connection is interrupted.

questions.prompt: The midbrain transmits signals in ____ directions.
questions.explanation: It transmits both ways.

questions.prompt: The hindbrain is responsible for basic ____ functions.
questions.explanation: It handles basic survival functions.

questions.prompt: The cerebellum is found ____ the cerebrum.
questions.explanation: It sits below the cerebrum.

questions.prompt: Once stored, learned movements run without input from the ____.
questions.explanation: They run without the cerebrum.

questions.prompt: Peristalsis is the wave-like ____ of muscles in the gut wall.
questions.explanation: It is wave-like muscle contraction.

questions.prompt: If the medulla stops working, ____ stops and the heart ceases to beat.
questions.explanation: Breathing stops without the medulla.

questions.prompt: The medulla connects the brain to the ____ ____.
questions.explanation: It connects the brain to the spinal cord.

questions.prompt: The pons is located in the ____ (brain division).
questions.explanation: The pons is in the hindbrain.

questions.prompt: The pons, midbrain and medulla together form the ____.
questions.explanation: They form the brainstem.

questions.prompt: The pituitary controls other ____ in the body.
questions.explanation: It controls other glands.

questions.prompt: The pituitary releases hormones that regulate growth, water balance and blood ____.
questions.explanation: It regulates growth, water and blood sugar.

questions.prompt: Sweating is the body's ____ to increased temperature.
questions.explanation: Sweating is a response.

questions.prompt: Animals' survival depends on how well they ____ to their surroundings.
questions.explanation: Survival depends on responding well.

questions.prompt: Receptors are specialized ____ that detect stimuli.
questions.explanation: Receptors are specialized cells/structures.

questions.prompt: When you touch a hot object, arm muscles ____ to pull the hand away.
questions.explanation: The arm muscles contract.

questions.prompt: Muscles produce the body's physical ____ to a stimulus.
questions.explanation: Muscles produce the physical response.

questions.prompt: A neuron is a thin and very ____ cell.
questions.explanation: Neurons are thin, long cells.

questions.prompt: Because dendrites only receive and axons only send, impulses are ____-way.
questions.explanation: Impulses are one-way.

questions.prompt: The cell body carries out the life functions of the ____.
questions.explanation: The cell body runs the neuron's life functions.

questions.prompt: A sensory neuron carries impulses from sense ____ to the CNS.
questions.explanation: From receptors to the CNS.

questions.prompt: A motor neuron causes muscles and glands to ____.
questions.explanation: Motor neurons make effectors respond.

questions.prompt: Myelin ensures signals travel along the correct ____.
questions.explanation: Myelin keeps signals on the correct pathway.

questions.prompt: Nerve fibres grouped together form a ____.
questions.explanation: Grouped fibres form a nerve.

questions.prompt: Reflex actions do not require a decision from the thinking ____.
questions.explanation: No decision from the thinking brain is needed.

questions.prompt: In a reflex, the ____ coordinates the response, not the brain.
questions.explanation: The spinal cord coordinates the reflex.

questions.prompt: Blinking and sneezing are examples of ____ actions.
questions.explanation: They are reflex actions.

questions.prompt: A flash of bright light makes the ____ become smaller.
questions.explanation: The pupil shrinks in bright light.

questions.prompt: The coughing reflex is essential because a blocked windpipe would stop ____.
questions.explanation: A blocked windpipe stops breathing.

questions.prompt: When you touch a newborn's palm, it curls its ____ and grips.
questions.explanation: The baby curls its fingers.

questions.prompt: Babies are born with reflexes because they cannot yet control their bodies ____.
questions.explanation: They lack voluntary control at birth.

questions.prompt: The neurotransmitter ____ across the synaptic gap.
questions.explanation: It diffuses across the gap.

questions.prompt: Thousands of synaptic connections create many possible ____.
questions.explanation: They create many pathways.

questions.prompt: A synapse allows a nerve impulse to pass from one neuron to the ____.
questions.explanation: It passes to the next neuron.

questions.prompt: When a nerve is cut, the related area may lose all ____.
questions.explanation: The area may lose all sensation.

questions.prompt: Because CNS nerves barely repair, nerve damage is often ____.
questions.explanation: CNS damage is often permanent.

questions.prompt: Vitamins are essential for nerve ____ function.
questions.explanation: Vitamins support nerve cell function.

questions.prompt: Neurotoxins can cause memory loss and permanent brain ____.
questions.explanation: They cause permanent brain damage.

questions.prompt: When blood sugar is very low, a person may feel confused or ____.
questions.explanation: Low blood sugar causes confusion or dizziness.

questions.prompt: The cerebrum controls muscles on the opposite ____ of the body.
questions.explanation: Each hemisphere controls the opposite side.

questions.prompt: The brain remains active even when we are ____.
questions.explanation: The brain stays active during sleep.

questions.prompt: Peristalsis helps move food during ____.
questions.explanation: It moves food during digestion.

questions.prompt: The full nervous system includes the brain, spinal cord, nerves, receptors and ____.
questions.explanation: All these form the complete nervous system.

questions.prompt: The cerebellum allows us to perform learned skills ____.
questions.explanation: Learned skills run automatically.

questions.prompt: The thalamus passes signals to the correct part of the ____.
questions.explanation: It routes signals to the cerebrum.

questions.prompt: The hypothalamus maintains a stable body ____.
questions.explanation: It keeps temperature stable.

questions.prompt: Receptors can detect light, which lets us have ____.
questions.explanation: Light detection gives vision.

questions.prompt: Axon terminals are the ____ branches of a neuron.
questions.explanation: They are the end branches.

questions.prompt: A reflex response happens without conscious ____ involvement.
questions.explanation: No conscious brain involvement is needed.

questions.prompt: The brain needs ____ as its main fuel for energy.
questions.explanation: Glucose is the main fuel.

questions.prompt: Growth hormone controls the ____ at which the body grows.
questions.explanation: It controls the growth rate.
